key_insight: A hybrid cross-modal attention model combines mammogram images with structured clinical data to improve early breast cancer detection in low-resource settings.
clinical_relevance: The approach is designed for hospitals with limited radiology expertise, aiming to support more accurate and locally relevant breast cancer screening in Ethiopia and similar contexts.
method: Trained a transformer-based cross-modal attention network on mammograms plus clinical variables.
Used a locally collected dataset from 1,024 patients across four Ethiopian referral hospitals.
Compared performance against image-only baselines and assessed robustness on lower-quality images.
evidence_signal: On 2,560 biopsy-confirmed mammograms, the model achieved 97.8% accuracy, 97.2% sensitivity, 98.3% specificity, and 0.987 AUC, with smaller performance drop on low-quality images than image-only models.
watch_item: Results come from a local retrospective dataset, so broader validation, workflow testing, and external generalization studies are still needed before deployment.
paper_title: Hybrid Cross-Modal Attention Network for Early Breast Cancer Detection in Low-Resource Clinical Settings
